title: One recompute, not fifty
summary: The dashboard report takes four seconds to build and fifty people open the dashboard every minute. Build the cache that computes it once for all of them, and once again when it goes stale, however many are waiting.

checkpoints.title: One computation for fifty callers
checkpoints.hint: Store the promise, not the value: put it in a map keyed by the cache key before you await it, and hand the same promise to everyone who arrives while it is there. Remove it when it settles, or the key is stuck on one computation forever.

checkpoints.title: A fresh value is not recomputed
checkpoints.hint: The deadline is set when the computation finishes and is never touched again, so reading a value does not extend its life. Compare against `clock.now()` on the way in rather than scheduling anything to delete it.

checkpoints.title: A failure is not a value
checkpoints.hint: Store the entry inside the success path only, and remove the in-flight promise however it settles: `finally` does both cases, `then` does one of them.

checkpoints.title: The stampede after expiry
checkpoints.hint: Expiry is the same cold-key path as the very first request, so if single-flight works there it works here. If fifty computations start, the check for an existing flight is happening after an await, and fifty callers have already gone past it.

checkpoints.title: The rules hold on schedules nobody wrote
checkpoints.hint: These schedules move the clock while a computation is in flight, which the other four never do, so `clock.now()` on the way into `get` and `clock.now()` when the computation finishes stop being the same number. Read the last line of the report first, because it names which rule went. If a value was rebuilt with time left on it, the deadline was taken from the wrong end: it runs from the moment the computation finished, not from when it started and not from when the caller arrived.
